articleTitle: A Simulation Algorithm of The Space-based Optical Star Map with Any Length of Exposure Time
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Aiming at the particularity of star tailing imaging under long exposure time, a simulation algorithm of the space-based optical star map with any length of exposure time is proposed. Firstly, the imaging process of the real space-based optical star map is introduced, and the imaging simulation process is designed. Then, by analyzing the limitations of traditional star tailing simulation algorithms, a star tailing simulation algorithm that adapts to long exposure time is proposed. And realized the simulation of space-based optical star map with any length of exposure time. The simulation experiment results show that this algorithm can simulate the star tailing images with any length of exposure time while ensuring the fidelity of imaging, which is of great significance to the development of space-based optical detection platforms.

articleTitle: Blast furnace chute visual detection based on mechanism model : Part 2: Numerical simulation of heat transfer in blast furnace chute
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The infrared thermal imager takes an image according to the temperature distribution of the object. Therefore, it is necessary to understand the temperature distribution of the chute before using infrared detection. The present paper is part 2 of a three paper series<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1][2]</sup> discussing the effect of high temperature gas flow on the chute temperature distribution. In this paper, the chute is numerically simulated and the distribution of chute temperature field is obtained. It provides a theoretical basis for effectively prolonging the service time of the chute. The results show that the high temperature gas flows around the chute during the charging process, resulting in metal chute heating. The chute is vulnerable to damage because of the impact of high temperature gas and the friction of charge particles.

articleTitle: Blast furnace chute visual detection based on mechanism model : Part 1: Analysis of chute wear based on discrete element method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Steel is one of the most important basic materials. More than 90% of steel in China comes from molten iron in blast furnace. The quality of blast furnace distribution chute directly affects the safety, longevity and efficient production of blast furnace. The bottom of the chute is impacted by the high temperature gas flow and the top part is worn by the charge particles. It is necessary and difficult to detect the damage of chute in real time. In this series of papers, the chute damage detection based on mechanism model by infrared imaging is discussed. Part 1 analyzes the impact of the charge particles on the chute. Part 2 focuses on the influence of the high temperature gas flow on the chute temperature distribution [1]. Part 3 discusses the infrared image processing method through the infrared image of the actual blast furnace [2]. In this paper, the reasons of chute damage are summarized. The movement of the particles in the chute is established by using the discrete element method, and the easily worn areas of the chute are obtained according to the motion trajectory of the burden. The calculation results lay a foundation for focusing the monitoring area by infrared.

articleTitle: Binary fringe pattern in infrared phase measuring deflectometry
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Infrared phase measuring deflectometry (IR PMD) is a superior PMD technique, which builds the direct relationship between phase and depth to directly calculate 3D shape of the non-continuous specular object from the phase data, instead of integrating the local slope data. IR PMD has been extensively studied because of its advantages of non-contact operation, high-precision measurement, and reducing influence of ambient light. However, there are certain requirements for the depth of field (DOF) in IR PMD system because many specular surfaces have large depth range. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a novel method based on defocusing binary fringes. This method combines binary fringe defocusing technique and IR PMD technique. This paper discusses the measurement principle and binary defocusing technique, and conducts simulated and practical experiments. The experimental results validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High-Speed and Accurate Method for the Gear Surface Integrity Detection Based on Visual Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In view of the defects of tooth profile defect and end face defect in the production process of injection gears due to the influence of technology, equipment and environment, there is an urgent need for rapid and accurate detection methods of gear surface integrity. In this paper, digital image processing technology is used to propose a rapid and accurate target matching detection method for the gear surface integrity based on normalized cross-correlation coefficients: First, the first derivative of the Gaussian function is used to construct a sub-pixel edge detector optimized based on the Canny operator to accurately extract the edge information of the gear to determine the target area; then, calculate the normalized correlation coefficient between the target area image and the template image, and realize the judgment of the surface integrity of the injection gear according to the matching coefficient threshold. The experimental results verify the feasibility and reliability of the algorithm. Its accuracy rate reaches 99.33%, and the detection time does not exceed 0.2s, which has a good industrial detection application value.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lidar Technology Development Based on Autonomous Driving Competition
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Autonomous driving is the future development trend, and the development of driverless racing competitions has promoted further innovation in autonomous vehicle technology. Based on the summary of the history of autonomous driving competitions at home and abroad, this paper constructs an automatic racing competition system model, analyzes the characteristics of lidar technology in autonomous driving competitions, and analyzes the development trend of lidar technology for autonomous driving racing.

articleTitle: A Novel Lightweight Infrared and Visible Image Fusion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Aiming at some usage scenarios that have strict requirements on the scale of fusion operation, this paper proposes a lightweight infrared and visible image fusion algorithm. The algorithm first uses bilateral filtering to decompose the image into the detail layer and the base layer. Secondly, the fusion of detail layers is achieved through regional variance. Then, the LC saliency detection method is performed on the original image to generate a saliency map. A weight map is generated from the saliency map of the original image to guide the base layer to perform fusion. Finally, the fusion image is obtained through linear transformation of the detail layer and the base layer. The proposed algorithm architecture is simplified, and only bilateral filtering is used to realize multi-scale decomposition, which reduces the operation scale. In terms of the fusion quality, after experimental verification, the proposed algorithm has certain advantages in the clarity and edge transition of the fused image compared with the comparison algorithm.

articleTitle: Synthesis of HgTe Quantum Dots and Its Application in Broadband Photodetection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Broadband photodetection from visible to infrared spectrum region are of increasing importance in military and civilian applications. Recently, mercury telluride (HgTe) colloidal quantum dots(CQDs) have gradually become an attractive alternative for traditional narrow band gap semiconductors owing to their tunable spectral response. In this paper, HgTe QDs have been successfully synthesized. By simply spin-coating and ligand exchange treatment, the broadband photodetection based on HgTe CQDs up to near Infrared can be achieved.

articleTitle: Blast furnace chute visual detection based on mechanism model : Part 3: Visual Detection Based on Infrared Images
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The present paper is part 3 of a paper series discussing the damage mechanism of blast furnace chute and the detection based on infrared imaging. While part 1 gives an overview on the effect of charge flow impact on blast furnace chute <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> and part 2 studies on the effect of high temperature gas flow on blast furnace chute <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup>. Based on the previous two parts of the study, we can predict the possible position of chute damage before monitoring, narrow the detection range, and lay a foundation for accurate detection. This third part discusses image processing of infrared image of blast furnace. The blast furnace chute is in constant motion, which makes the automatic detection of infrared thermal imaging on top of blast furnace based on image processing become a difficult task. According to different thermodynamic coefficient and temperature, the image of each part of the furnace top is different. The features of damaged chute areas are extracted by means of image processing methods such as median filtering, histogram equalization, thresholding and image multiplication. It is necessary to combine the prediction of mechanism model with visual image to determine whether the abnormal temperature area is consistent with the vulnerable area, otherwise there will be misjudgment.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Detection Module for the Chromatic Confocal Measurement Sensor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Chromatic confocal microscopy (CCM) has the advantages of high accuracy, strong anti-interference ability and sensitivity to objects with low reflectivity. Its disadvantage is that it needs to measure all points on the surface of the measured object, which is an inefficient measurement. Currently, domestic researches mostly focuses on the development of dispersed objective lens, the research on improving the measurement efficiency is not enough. This article introduces a method that can improve the efficiency of CCM measurement. It uses hardware to accelerate the calculation of the decoding algorithm, which not only speeds up the signal processing time but also reduces a lot of data transmission time. The hardware used for acceleration is a photo-detector driven by field-programmable gate array (FPGA). This paper also designed the optical path in front of the photo detector, which can make the photo detector receive accurate spectral information. Through calculation and simulation, our method can ensure accuracy and increase the measurement speed of CCM.

articleTitle: Fast Stereo Matching Method Based on Two-step AD-Census Fusion
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: With the development of industrial information technology, an online industrial quality inspection technology which can make the computer quickly and efficiently obtain the 3D information of the industrial production line environment is particularly important. With the development of computer technology and the extensive application of stereo matching technology, more and more industrial inspection systems have adopted online monitoring programs such as binocular stereo vision. Due to the shortage of the traditional stereo matching algorithm, such as complicated process and demanding hardware conditions, a fast AD-Census stereo matching algorithm was proposed in this paper, combining the idea of image pyramid, aiming at the characteristics of large resolution and high demand on algorithm efficiency of industrial online inspection. In this paper, AD algorithm is simple and fast, Census algorithm is insensitive to illumination difference and has high robustness to edge information and makes full use of the idea that multi-scale pyramid pays attention to the main trend, which can achieve a higher efficiency of stereo matching algorithm without too much loss of accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of test system for gun stabilization accuracy
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In order to improve the test accuracy and efficiency for gun stabilization accuracy, a test system using CCD and standard target was designed. First, the composing and test principle of the system were introduced. According to the request of the system indexes, the main frame parameters of the optical system were analyzed and confirmed; the optical system was designed concretely and optimized using the wave-deviation method and the ZEMAX software. Then, the vehicle image recording and control unit was designed using high speed and great capacity storage technique, and its main technique indexes were analyzed. Finally, the main performance indexes of the test system were analyzed and validated by test. The test result indicates the test accuracy precedes 0.07mil, and the performance parameters meet the indexes request.

articleTitle: Discussion of cross-axis isolation in vector atomic magnetometry via longitudinal field modulation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Atomic magnetometry based on longitudinal field modulation allows transverse x-and y-components measurement of a magnetic field simultaneously. In this paper, cross-axis isolation between these two-axis components is derived and investigated mathematically. An analytical model is established to optimize the cross-axis isolation during the transversal components measurement. By manipulating the amplitude and the frequency of the longitudinal field modulation, two transverse magnetic field components could be divided completely. The proposed technique plays significant role in optimization of vectoral atomic magnetometry.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Influence of Thickener Type on the Reflux Characteristics of Grease under Starved Lubrication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The grease film thickness is measured on the nano scale Elastohydrodynamic (EHL) test rig based on optical interferometry. Under the experimental conditions, the contact area experiences the lubrication states of full lubrication, starved lubrication and film thickness recovery. Compared with the polyurea grease, the lithium grease enters into the starved lubrication much earlier and the film thickness is lower in starved lubrication. However, the film thickness of lithium grease also rises earlier and the rising amplitude is larger than the polyurea grease. The deficiency degree with thickener type of lithium is more serious than polyurea while the reflux capacity of lithium grease is much better than polyurea grease.

articleTitle: Characterizing static aberration in reflective liquid crystal spatial light modulators (LC-SLM) using random phase shifting interferometry
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: To accurate modulate the phase of the incoming light, the backplane aberration of a spatial light modulator (SLM) needs to be measured and compensated. In this paper, we develop an interferometric method to calibrate the static aberration. In our method, a Michelson interferometer was constructed and the SLM itself was used to produce the random phase shift that we need. In addition, the phase demodulation method based on matrix VU factorization (VU) and phase unwrapping algorithm based on derivative Zernike polynomial fitting (DZPT) are adopted to get the phase profile of the static aberration. Experimental result shows that our proposed method can get a pretty good compensation result.

articleTitle: Creating Seed Coat Catalog Using Spectral Domain Optical Coherence Tomography
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: As a non-destructive method, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) has already been adapted to study seed samples. SD-OCT provides a set of capabilities in terms of millimetre-scale penetration depth, high-speed acquisition, and resolution typically in the range of ten microns. It has been therefore gaining popularity in this specific field. However, only a limited number of seed cultivars have been investigated with OCT so far, and there has been little discussions about the applicability of the OCT to other seed varieties. In this work, we report the measurement of 14 types of seed using OCT system. It was found that OCT can provide high-resolution cross-sectional images of 12 out of 14 seed types. This work represents the first systematic study towards a seed catalog which provides the essential information about the applicability of OCT for studying a variety.

articleTitle: A Neural Network-based Method for Fast Angle Calibration of MEMS LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: MEMS LiDAR has been drawing more and more attention as a representative achievement in low power consumption and miniaturization integration of LiDAR research. To address the problem that traditional angle calibration methods for mechanical LiDAR are not completely applicable in MEMS LiDAR due to different sources of angle errors, a neural network-based method for fast angle calibration of MEMS LiDAR is proposed. The calibration field only consists of a rotating platform and an angular reflector. By modelling the calibration field and analyzing the error sources of MEMS LiDAR, including the mounting error, the nonlinear error, and the systematic error, a neural network model was then developed to correct the angle measurement errors. The experimental results show that the method is reasonable and effective and is able to achieve fast angle calibration of MEMS LiDAR.

articleTitle: Quantitative relationship study between spatial heterogeneity and uncertainty of high-resolution pixel scale based on spectral measurement simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In the validation of high-resolution pixel scale reflectance, the uncertainty of point-to-plane scaling is an important constraint factor in getting the reference true value of pixel-scale. The spatial heterogeneity of the surface is the cause of it. The quantitative relationship between them can provide guidance for the quantitative calculation of the scaling uncertainty in the validation, and reference for site selection and sampling optimization. This paper proposes a spectral measurement simulation and scaling uncertainty calculation method based on UAV high-resolution images. The quantitative relationship between spatial heterogeneity and scaling uncertainty is analyzed, and the influence of sampling method, sampling number and plane scale on the relationship is discussed. The gray-scale value is used as the reference of reflectivity. The results show that the relationships of different sampling schemes are consistent, the cv is significantly positive correlation with the average scaling uncertainty, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is above 0.98; Random sampling has larger scaling uncertainty than system sampling, and the smaller number of sampling points and the larger the plane scale, the larger the scaling uncertainty.

articleTitle: Image Reconstruction of Photonics Integrated Interference Imaging System: stablized CLEAN methods
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Photonics Integrated Interference Imaging System (PIIIS) is a recently developed far-filed imaging approach aiming at high imaging performance and compact structure. Several sampling lenslet arrays have been proposed to acquire higher imaging quality. These lens configurations provide low-frequency intensive but high-frequency sparse measurements of complex visibility. However, this kind of sampling will induce Gibbs-ringing artifacts in inverse Fourier images. In this article, entropy prior and smoothness prior are proposed to remove the ringing artifacts, and stabilized CLEAN algorithms based on those priors are used to reconstruct images. A simulation experiment using hierarchical multistage sampling lens array is implemented, and the results show that these algorithms can eliminate the ringing artifacts.

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Robot for Bank Early Warning and Security Based on Robot Vision
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In today's society, automated teller machine robberies continue to occur. Based on the comparison of various monitoring systems, this paper has produced a bank early warning security intelligent robot based on robot vision, which will detect the target's actions in real time, and will automatically alarm once an abnormality occurs to ensure the personal safety of users. At the same time, in order to improve the use in different situations, combined with machine vision to provide gesture recognition, and use wavelet transform, gaussian denoising, template comparison and other digital algorithms in the image fusion process to improve the accuracy of recognition for the robot in different environments .

articleTitle: Nonlinearity suppression method for optical frequency scanning based on the Phenomenological model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The frequency-scanning interferometer’s (FSI) precision relies much on its tunable laser source. The external cavity laser diode (ECDL) is an ideal choice for FSI due to its narrow linewidth and high tuning speed. However, ECLD exhibits nonlinearity during optical frequency scanning produced by the inherent hysteresis effect in the piezo-electric transducer (PZT) ceramic. The interference signal hence becomes nonstationary, and the phase extracting of the interference signal causes errors. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel method based on the asymmetric Prandtl–Ishlinskii (API) model for nonlinearity suppression of optical frequency scanning. By taking the linear driving signal and instantaneous optical frequency of the ECLD as input and output data of the model respectively, then, the hysteresis model can be obtained by using the API modelling method. The model’s inverse then can be employed as a feedforward controller to suppress the nonlinearity of the optical frequency scanning. In this case, a corrected waveform of the PZT driving signal is implemented instead of linear driving signal to suppress the nonlinear frequency scanning of the ECDL. The results of simulation validate the effectiveness of the proposed suppression method with root-square-mean-error (RMS) of 1.6357×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> GHz.

articleTitle: Autostereoscopic Measurement System for Rapid 3D Inspection of Wire Bonding
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The quality of wire bonding is an important factor in the manufacturing of various precision electronic components in semiconductor industry. The wire bonding defects, including high loop and low loop, determined by the bonding height information, inevitably affect the performance of the product. It is vital to measure height information quickly and accurately to reduce the failure rate in the manufacturing process. However, traditional measurement system often needs to move the target samples for a number of times. To address the key measurement problems, a three-dimensional (3D) optical measurement system is developed based on autostereoscopy technologies. A micro-lens array is used to divide the light emitted by the sample into different directions. The elemental images from different view angles contain original 3D information and is recorded by a high-resolution image sensor. On the basis of the multi-view stereo information contained in the image, the elemental images can be refocused into multi-focus images. The 3D information can be directly extracted from the multi-focus images through self-developed algorithms. Experiment results show that the system can complete the measurement in 2 seconds and reach a high measurement accuracy at a sub-micrometer level. This verifies the feasibility of the proposed measurement system which is efficient and accurate for 3D inspection of wire bonding.

articleTitle: An Accelerated Algorithm for 3D Reconstruction of Groove Structure Based on Parallel Light and White Light Interference
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: We propose a three-dimensional image reconstruction acceleration algorithm based on parallel light white light interference system. We move the sample or mirror to be tested longitudinally to adjust the optical path, and then, collect and number the interference images in the 2um range near the position of the sample surface where the interference fringes are obvious. The group’s images around the upper and lower surfaces which are the interference images with the largest contrast in each group of images are partially reconstructed in 3D. Use the contrast information to segment the interference images with the largest contrast in each group of images collected, ensure that each sub-region can contain the maximum and minimum values of interference fringes on the iso-optical path surface. The contrast is compared with the contrast of the entire image, and the position of the iso-optical path surface is extracted, and the local 3D reconstruction results are spliced using the obtained position of the iso-optical path surface to complete the overall 3D shape detection. The reconstruction result of the algorithm in this paper is significantly improved compared with the reconstruction result directly using the differential centroid method. In terms of speed, the reconstruction time of the algorithm in this paper is 0.0429s, and the reconstruction time directly using the differential centroid method. is 1.540s.

articleTitle: Towards a Novel Phase Unwrapping Model for Three Dimensional Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In order to obtain a higher quantity absolute phase, a novel phase unwrapping model by combination of dual-frequency heterodyne and segmented quantifization phase coding method is proposed in this research. This model also provides a generalized phase order error correction method for eliminate phase order jump errors. Only ten fringe patterns are used for the projection in this study. The workflow of the devised model starts with acquisition of the low frequency wrapped phase by using the classic double-frequency heterodyne method, and then it moves to obtain the fringe order of low frequency wrapped phase based on the projected segmented quantifization phase coding patterns. In this step, two-dimensional scanning lookup method is used to eliminate the noise points caused by the rounding operation. Then, new fringe order can be obtained by combination of the obtained fringe order of low frequency wrapped phase and the new projected binary fringe pattern with complementarity, and this new fringe order combined with the previous fringe order can be used to unwrap the heterodyne phase. Finally, the wrapped phase of the dual-frequency is unwrapped through unwrapped heterodyne phase and the highest frequency phase. This study applies metal workpiece measurements as case studies to test the validity of the proposed model. The experimental results show that the error effects of fringe order can be eliminated, and the high frequency fringes retain more information on the measure workpiece surfaces.

articleTitle: The measurement of the center of mass and the optical center in a freely falling body of absolute gravimetry
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In absolute gravimeters, rotation of the falling body leads to inaccurate measurement of gravity. The error can be minimized by collocating the center of mass (COM) of the body with its optical center (OC). A method to measure the distance between these centers is necessary. The method is based on torsion pendulum device. This paper considers the falling body as a pendulum in the whole system and using a quadrature interferometer to interrogate its twist mode.

articleTitle: Design of readout circuit chip for medium wave 640 × 512-25um IRFPA
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: This paper reports a new readout integrated circuit designed for hybridization with P-on-N detector such as InSb, HgCdTe and InGaAs, and it can support a wide range of system through flexibility and versatile functions. This ROIC is fabricated using CSMC 0.18um double poly, six metal process that utilized high-speed CMOS transistors. The device can work at temperatures of 80K with 5.5V supply voltage. It still has a build-in temperature sensor to detect the temperature of the chip. The pixel cell occupies an area of 25×25µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with an input charge-handling of 18Me<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> carriers. After testing at 80K, the output swing was larger than 3V; the power consumption of chip was about 180mW; the output noise was about 400uV and its dynamic range was about 78dB.

articleTitle: Distributed design of wind tunnel temperature test system based on CAN bus
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The CAN bus distributed temperature test system for the wind tunnel is proposed in this paper due to the disadvantages of VXI and PXI bus test system for the on site wind tunnel temperature test, low precision for the long-distance transmission, reliability and test ability limitation. We elaborate the basic principle of hardware design and software design described in details. The reliability and stability of the temperature test system is tested via the wind tunnel experiment, which shows that the CAN bus distributed temperature test system has the feature of stable process, reliable performance and high precision.

articleTitle: Fabrication of large-sized stitching computer generated hologram (CGH)
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: With the rapid development of astronomical observation, segmented telescopes with large equivalent aperture have attracted much attentions. However, it is an urgent problem to realize high-precision optical co-phase among sub-mirrors of the segmented telescope. High-accuracy and large-sized computer-generated holograms (CGHs) are expected to guide the co-phase alignment of sub-mirrors. Meanwhile, the large-sized CGHs are required with the enlarged aperture of telescopes. At present, it is hard to fabricate large-sized CGHs by traditional processing methods. In this paper, a stitching method is proposed to fabricate large-sized CGHs.

articleTitle: A Phased Landmark Navigation Method for Lunar Exploration
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: This paper proposes a phased landmark navigation method for the pinpoint landing problem during lunar exploration, which divides the navigation process into two phases: control landmarks phase and random landmarks phase. The control landmarks are ground markers containing terrain information extracted from the topographic map of the known landing area, and the random landmarks are image markers extracted between successive images of the spacecraft. In the control landmark phase, the control landmarks are matched with the images taken during the spacecraft landing for localization. To ensure that the control point positions on each landing image frame are extracted accurately, this paper first passes the position of the control points between adjacent frames by homograph transformation and splits small template images near the positions to match the template images with the control landmarks for template matching and search for the sub-pixel image point positions. The last landing image that can match with the control landmarks is used as the reference map in the random landmarks phase, and Harris feature points are extracted on the subsequent landing images to make random landmarks and then matched with the reference map for positioning. Finally, the method is verified using the images taken by Chang’e-4 landing camera and the terrain data of 5m resolution in the landing area. The experimental results show that this method can effectively increase the working range of visual navigation and achieve a pinpoint landing accuracy of about 10m at the same time.

articleTitle: Design of the Telecentric Lens for Dual Side Imaging of the Small Size Particles with Equal Optical Path
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Due to the industrial automation requirements, a machine vision is widely used in the industrial production and detection. Compared with the traditional artificial, it has the advantages of high speed and high accuracy, especially to the small-size granular products. It is difficult to detect the surfaces of the small-size granular products quickly and accurately by artificial vision due to the limitations of human eyes. Therefore, the machine vision system with large magnification and high resolution often being used. For the products that need to detect multiple surface, it is often necessary to configure multiple sets of machine vision systems, which are very complex. In order to realize the multi-surfaces detection of small-size granular products, a two-sided imaging telecentric optical lens is designed in this paper, which can image the adjacent surfaces of the product simultaneously using one set of machine vision system. The lens consists of five prisms for double-sided image conversion and splitting and six spherical lenses. It has 1 times magnification, high resolution and the telecentricity was less than 0.01 °， the working distance is 36.84mm. Because there is an inclined angle of the glass wedge in the meridian plane, which makes the meridian plane asymmetric, when the MTF value is 0.3, the Nyquist frequency of the meridian surface is 65 lp/mm, and the Nyquist frequency of the sagittal surface is 125 lp/mm. The maximum distortion of the system is controlled within 0.2%, and it is suitable for 2 / 3 "CCD. Through tolerance analysis, the lens has good tolerance compatibility, high cost performance, and can be mass produced.

articleTitle: Test system of laser ultrasonic directional transmission channel characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In order to enhance the transmission efficiency of laser ultrasonic signal and realize laser ultrasonic directional transmission, a channel characteristic test system based on double sliding window algorithm is designed in this paper. This paper analyzes the principle of laser ultrasonic directional transmission, selects the double-sided band modulation mode, and obtains the differential frequency wave sound pressure generated by the nonlinear interaction according to the Lighthill sound scattering principle; obtains the laser ultrasonic directional transmission efficiency parameters by calculating the differential frequency sound intensity after the air nonlinear interaction, and creates the preconditions for the construction of the system; and through the channel impulse response detection algorithm.The CIR vector is obtained by using the local PN sequence and the peak value generated by the received signal, the threshold value is determined based on the double sliding window algorithm, the end position of the interval is determined, the accuracy of channel estimation is improved, and the error code performance of the system is improved; the full digital DQPSK is demodulated by using FPGA and DSP devices, and the channel characteristic test system is constructed by using the analog-to-digital conversion plate and the interface plate. The simulation results show that the designed system can effectively improve the transmission accuracy of the laser ultrasonic audio channel, and the system has a high efficiency of data reception, strong practicability and robustness.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks’ Applications in Automatic Target Recognition for Synthetic Aperture Images
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) is an important research area in the field of radar information processing. Because the deep Convolution Neural Network (CNN) does not need to carry out feature engineering and the performance of image classification is superior, it attracts more and more attention in the field of radar automatic target recognition. The application of CNN to radar image processing is reviewed in this paper. Firstly, the related knowledges including the characteristics of the radar image is introduced, and the limitations of traditional radar automatic target recognition methods are pointed out. The principle, composition and development of CNN the field of computer vision are introduced. Then, the research status of CNN in radar automatic target recognition is provided. The detection and recognition method of SAR image are presented in detail. Then, the challenge of radar automatic target recognition is analyzed. Finally, the new theory and model of convolution neural network, the new imaging technology of radar and the application to complex environments in the future are prospected.

articleTitle: An object recognition method based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Deep learning's self-learning capabilities are used to identify objects. Based on the traditional CNN convolutional neural network, this paper constructs a new network model, in which the 9 linear stacked inception modules are embedded. The use of inception modules reuses more features, improves the width of feature tensors, optimizes the training speed and improves the detection accuracy. Firstly, food picture data source is constructed and preprocessed. Then, some images are used to train the model, and the optimization algorithm SGDM is used to update the parameters, and the influence of learning rate on the training effect of the model is compared. Finally, the model is tested by testing the food pictures in the test data set, and the simulation based on MATLAB shows that the model improves the efficiency and accuracy of object recognition. It reflects the potential and advantages of deep learning in feature extraction.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Influence of Macro-micro Grating Parameters on Diffraction Characteristics through FDTD Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The grating is the displacement measurement standard, and the diffraction efficiency of the diffracted light of the grating mainly determines the accuracy of the displacement measurement system. In this work, through three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method simulation, the diffraction efficiency of the ±1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order diffracted light of the transmission diffraction grating under different macro complex groove types and micro surface roughness is studied, and the optimal groove type and surface roughness parameters were obtained. The research results provide a basis for the optimal design of grating manufacturing.

articleTitle: A fast point cloud precision registration method based on spatial grid division
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Point cloud precision registration is the most time-consuming link in registration, and the main factor that hinders point cloud registration from meeting the real-time requirement. In this paper we propose a fast point cloud precision registration method based on spatial grid division. By virtue of the spatial grid, the scattered point cloud is transformed into the spatial grid sequence. During the applicaton of the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm, we can get the neighborhood information of any point with the aid of the neighborhood information of the grid sequence to efficiently determine the nearest neighbor points. When calculating the nearest neighbor points, the grids don’t interfere with each other. Hence, we can use GPU parallel processing to accelerate the search of the nearest neighbor points. Spatial grid division and parallel processing greatly improve registration efficiency.

articleTitle: Building Damage Detection Method Based on Normal Vector Computation of Airborne Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Earthquake is one of the major natural disaster which endangers the existence and development of mankind. The collapse of buildings caused by earthquake is one of the important reasons causing the casualties. Therefore, it is very important to recognize and extract the damage of buildings quickly. Airborne LiDAR can acquire high resolution point cloud data, which can provide height or other information for building damage detection. This paper finds an effective factor which can be used to detect building damage when we only have post-earthquake point cloud data. The factor is an angle, which is calculated from the normal vector and zenith of point cloud data. Through the test of large scale of point cloud data, the Kappa coefficient is 0.788, which proves the validity of this method. The result provides new ideas for the detection of building damage type and damage degree.

articleTitle: Calibration method for measuring angle device with CCD
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Angle measuring accuracy is the important technique index of the measuring angle device with CCD. The calibration methods for CCD camera have some disadvantages, such as the high requirements to the used devices and the complicated operation processes. This paper proposed a new calibration method based on the triangle principle using cross target, the corresponding mathematics model is established. The results of the academic analysis and the contrast experiment show that the new method is correct, and its accuracy can be controlled. It is easy to be popularized and applied because of the strong adaptability and the simple operation.

articleTitle: Active Millimeter Wave Imaging based on CGC Lens
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Millimeter wave (MMW) focal plane imaging systems based on traditional polymer lenses are generally of poor imaging quality. In this work, we introduce a cage-shaped granules of conductor (CGC) lens into an active millimeter wave (AMMW) focal plane imaging system and evaluate the focusing performance of CGC lens. Imaging tests are performed on different mental objects including concealed dagger carried by human body, and the imaging quality is acceptable.

articleTitle: Research on OCT Imaging Law of Frozen Meat Applied with Electric Field During Storage
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: It has always been the points of interests in the field of food science about how to quickly and non-destructively detect the quality of frozen meat. Among these issues, storage period of frozen meat is the hard one to infer, this study makes a preliminary exploration. We use optical coherence tomography (OCT) technology to visualize the reaction of the meat with low-frequency AC electric field applied. We calculate the average correlation coefficient (ACC), which is based on the two-dimensional correlation map between frames of OCT images, both before and after sample being electrified. It is proved that there is a significant difference in ACC with and without external electric field, and this difference increases with the extension of frozen storage period. It is worth mentioning that this study takes the frozen storage period of meat as a variable to discuss the imaging characteristics of electro-kinetic response of meat. It laid a foundation for the future application of inversing the storage period of frozen meat.

articleTitle: Two-frame phase extraction technology based on vector normalization with single filter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: This paper presents a fast and direct phase extraction method for two-frame fringe patterns. First, perform addition and subtraction operations on the two frames of phase shift fringe images, and only need to perform a single high-pass filter on the addition result to obtain a set of sine and cosine components. Then use the vector normalization method to achieve the vector orthogonality of the sine and cosine components. Finally, the phase to be measured of the interference fringe pattern is obtained by arctangent operation. The algorithm is compact in structure and efficient in processing. The accuracy and efficiency of the method are verified by comparing simulations with different methods and testing of experimental interferograms.

articleTitle: Form Recognition Based on Lightweight U-Net and Tesseract after Multi-level Retraining
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet information technology and the advancement of enterprise digitization, the digitization of paper forms has also received extensive attention. The automatic conversion of paper form documents into electronic form documents mainly faces three problems. The first is that the format of the form file is diverse and the structure is complex. This article uses the XML file of the form to accurately analyze the structure of the file, which is more accurate than the current semantic segmentation method. The second problem is table area detection, this paper uses traditional algorithms to find the contours of the candidate table area, and screens according to the characteristics of the table area to complete the detection and extraction of the table area. The third is that the recognition of the table text is more difficult, not only the interference information such as the table frame will also affect the accuracy of text recognition, and the type of text information in the table is complex, including Chinese, English, numbers, symbols and mixed types, which bring huge challenges to text recognition. This paper uses the lightweight U-Net network model to segment the text area at pixel level, eliminating the interference information of text recognition. The neural network of Tesseract was retrained in a multiple, multi-level manner, and successfully realized the recognition of complex types of text information with an accuracy of about 96%. Based on deep learning and XML table structure analysis algorithm, this paper realizes the recognition of paper version of the form file and the reconstruction of the electronic version of the file.

articleTitle: Error analysis of a photoelastic-modulated Mueller matrix ellipsometer
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: As a complex optical measurement system, the potoelastic-modulated Mueller matrix ellipsometer (PMME) inevitably suffers from errors in the process of system calibration and measurement. Due to the inevitability and universality of the error, the error analysis is an indispensable link in the development of the instrument. In this article, the source and classification of errors in the instrument are analyzed systematically at first. Then, based on the error propagation theory, the error transfer model of the instrument is established. Through a series of error transfer simulation experiments, the influence of various errors on the measurement accuracy and precision of Mueller matrix is quantitatively analyzed.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Following-based Binocular Vision Method for the Deformation Measurement of Motion Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference of Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Motion load-bearing structures are widely used in aerospace and marine heavy industries, while the means to measure the deformation of kinematic structures are limited. In response to some shortcomings of the current motion structure deformation measurement methods, this paper proposes a large-field-of-view, high-precision, and universal kinematic structure deformation measurement method based on dynamic following and dynamic vision measurement technologies, and introduces its principle, measurement steps and measurement considerations in detail. Moreover, the effect of acceleration on the highly stable structure in the dynamic following module was evaluated by finite element software. The results show that the acceleration has a great influence on the overall deformation of the high stability structure, but its influence on the measurement accuracy is limited.
